title: Best Payment Gateway for Travel Agencies and Websites in 2026
summary: Learn how to choose a payment gateway for a travel agency or booking website, including split settlements, refunds, international payments and reconciliation.

Travel payment infrastructure is not the same as retail payment infrastructure. A customer may book a holiday months before travelling. The amount may then need to be settled with a hotel, transport provider or other supplier on different timelines. If the booking is cancelled, the business may need to process a full or partial refund and reconcile it against the original reservation.


International bookings add another layer. Travel websites may need to accept international cards, present prices in the customer’s preferred currency, settle funds in INR and maintain the documentation required for cross-border receipts.


A standard gateway can process the checkout. A payment platform suited to travel should also support the operational workflows surrounding the booking. This guide explains what travel agencies and booking websites should evaluate when selecting one.


##


Why Travel Businesses May Be Treated as High-Risk Merchants


Payment providers may apply closer scrutiny to travel businesses because of three structural characteristics:


- **Long fulfilment window:** A customer may pay in January for a trip in July. This creates a longer period during which a cancellation, dispute or chargeback can arise before the service is delivered.
- **High average booking values:** International holidays, group tours and bundled packages can involve large transactions. When combined with delayed fulfilment, this increases the potential financial exposure associated with refunds and disputes.
- **Fraud and card-testing risk:** Travel bookings can attract fraudulent transactions because of their high value and digital fulfilment journey. Real-time risk checks, device and behavioural signals, velocity rules and appropriate card authentication can help reduce this exposure.


Depending on the merchant’s risk profile, transaction history and payment provider, processing fees for a travel business may be 20–30% higher than standard retail rates. This is not a universal surcharge: actual pricing, reserve requirements and settlement terms are determined during underwriting.


For an Indian travel business, the payment provider should have the appropriate RBI authorisation for the services it offers. Cross-border collections also require the relevant regulatory framework and documentation. PCI DSS compliance and secure authentication should be considered baseline requirements for handling card payments.


##


What a Payment Gateway for Travel Agencies Must Handle


Beyond standard checkout capabilities, travel businesses should evaluate how a gateway supports these industry-specific workflows.


### Advance deposits and balance collection


Many travel bookings involve an initial deposit followed by one or more balance payments. The payment setup should allow the agency to collect these amounts separately and associate every transaction with the correct booking.


[Cashfree Payment Links](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) allow businesses to create and share payment links through channels such as WhatsApp, SMS or email. This can be useful when a traveller needs to pay a deposit or an outstanding balance without returning to the booking website.


For genuinely recurring payment arrangements, UPI AutoPay can be considered where the use case and mandate structure are suitable. A scheduled balance for a single trip should not automatically be treated as a subscription; the collection method should match the booking and customer-consent flow.


### Multi-vendor payment splits


A package booking may involve a hotel, transport operator, activity provider and the travel agency itself. Manually calculating commissions and releasing each supplier payment increases operational work and reconciliation risk.


[Cashfree Easy Split](https://www.cashfree.com/easy-split/split-payment-gateway/) enables businesses to collect a customer payment, deduct commissions and configure settlements to vendors or partners. It also supports refund-related adjustments in vendor settlements.


The exact flow depends on the commercial relationship between the agency and its suppliers. Before implementation, the business should confirm onboarding, settlement and compliance requirements for each vendor type.


### Refunds and cancellations


Travel bookings frequently involve cancellations, date changes and partial refunds. A suitable gateway should support full and partial refunds against the original transaction, provide clear refund-status updates and expose webhooks or APIs that keep the booking system in sync.


Automation can reduce manual processing, but the refund amount must still follow the agency’s published cancellation policy and supplier terms. Quick acknowledgement and transparent timelines can also reduce the likelihood of customers escalating a refund request into a payment dispute.


### International payments


Indian travel businesses serving overseas customers may need to accept international cards and display prices in multiple currencies. The payment provider should clearly explain supported currencies, settlement currency, expected timelines and cross-border documentation.


Cashfree’s[International Payment Gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/international-payment-gateway/) supports international cards and payments in 140+ currencies. International payments are generally settled in INR to the registered bank account, typically within T+2 business days, subject to onboarding, risk checks and the applicable service terms.


Cashfree Payments states that it is authorised as a PA-CB for export and import transactions. Businesses should still confirm whether their specific travel service, transaction model and purpose code are supported before going live.


### Booking-level reconciliation


A travel agency processing hundreds or thousands of transactions needs to match each payment with the right booking, traveller and outstanding amount. Relying only on bank-statement narration can create delays and errors.


[Cashfree Smart Collect](https://www.cashfree.com/virtual-account/) uses virtual accounts and virtual UPI IDs to help businesses identify incoming bank transfers and reconcile them with customers or orders. Depending on the implementation, a travel company can map a virtual payment identifier to a booking, customer or corporate account.


##


Payment Methods That Matter for Travel Websites in India


The ideal payment mix depends on booking value, customer location and whether the booking is for an individual or a company. Travel websites should usually consider the following options.


### UPI


UPI is an important payment method for domestic bookings because it provides a familiar, mobile-first payment experience. Cashfree’s[UPI Payment Gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-payment-gateway/) supports intent, dynamic QR, WhatsApp UPI links and collect flows. Transaction eligibility and limits can vary by bank, customer profile and the rules applicable to the specific flow, so businesses should not assume every high-value booking can be completed through UPI.


***Also read:[How to Integrate a UPI Payment Gateway into a Website](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/upi-integration/)***


### Credit and debit cards


Cards remain important for high-value purchases, corporate travel and international customers. The gateway should support major card networks relevant to the business and provide secure authentication and fraud controls for card-not-present transactions.


### Card EMI


EMI can make high-value packages more manageable for eligible customers. Travel businesses should check supported issuers, eligibility rules, tenures, pricing and whether standard or no-cost EMI is available for their merchant category.


### Net banking


Net banking remains useful for customers who prefer direct bank payments and for some corporate booking workflows. Coverage across commonly used banks and clear payment-status updates are important for reconciliation.


### International cards and wallets


Overseas travellers may expect to use an international card or supported wallet. These transactions require additional fraud monitoring and cross-border compliance. Businesses should confirm supported markets, currencies, card networks and settlement terms during onboarding.


### UPI AutoPay


[UPI AutoPay](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-upi-autopay/) is designed for recurring collections based on a customer-approved mandate. It may suit travel memberships, recurring corporate arrangements or other repeat-payment products, but it is not automatically the right option for every deposit-and-balance booking.


Cashfree’s Payment Gateway supports 180+ domestic and international payment modes, including UPI, cards, EMI options, net banking and wallets. Actual availability may depend on merchant approval, customer eligibility and the payment method selected.


##


Security and Compliance Requirements for Travel Payments


Travel payment security operates across several layers. A travel business should evaluate both the provider’s credentials and the controls available within its own integration.


### PCI DSS compliance


PCI DSS defines security requirements for organisations that store, process or transmit cardholder data. Using a[PCI DSS-compliant](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/pci-dss-compliance-requirements-checklist/) payment provider can reduce the amount of sensitive card data that reaches the travel business’s systems, although the merchant’s own compliance responsibilities depend on its integration model.


### Secure card authentication


3D Secure 2.x supports risk-based authentication for online card payments. Depending on the card, issuer and transaction, a low-risk payment may have a lower-friction flow while a higher-risk transaction may require additional verification. International card acceptance and authentication availability should be confirmed for the target markets.


### RBI authorisation


For domestic online payment aggregation, businesses should verify that the provider holds the appropriate RBI Payment Aggregator authorisation. When an Indian business accepts cross-border payments through an aggregator, it should also check the provider’s PA-CB authorisation and whether the proposed transaction falls within the supported export or import framework.


### FEMA and cross-border documentation


Indian travel businesses receiving overseas payments must correctly classify and document cross-border receipts. Requirements may include the appropriate purpose code and remittance documentation, depending on the transaction.


Cashfree’s international payment solutions provide settlement and cross-border reporting features, including FIRC-related reporting for supported flows. The exact document provided can differ by product and transaction structure, so businesses should confirm documentation requirements during onboarding instead of assuming the same certificate applies to every international booking.


***Also read:[Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate: Meaning, Uses and How to Obtain It](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/)***


### Fraud prevention


The[gateway should support real-time risk screening](https://www.cashfree.com/risk-shield-payment-gateway/) , velocity rules and transaction monitoring. A travel business should also apply its own controls, such as verifying unusual itinerary changes, reviewing mismatches between traveller and payer details, limiting repeated attempts and maintaining clear evidence of booking acceptance and service delivery.

Payment failures and abandoned checkout sessions can result in lost bookings even when the traveller intends to pay.[Cashfree Relay](https://www.cashfree.com/relay/) is designed to support workflows such as recovering abandoned carts and retrying failed payments. Travel platforms should assess availability and integration fit against their booking-confirmation logic before adopting it.


##


How to Choose the Right Payment Gateway for a Travel Business


Before selecting a provider, compare the following factors against the way your business actually accepts and fulfils bookings:


1. **Business-model approval:** Confirm that the provider supports your travel category, fulfilment timeline and supplier structure.
2. **Payment-method coverage:** Prioritise the methods used by your domestic, corporate and international customers.
3. **Refund workflow:** Check support for full and partial refunds, status tracking, APIs and webhooks.
4. **Vendor settlement model:** Determine whether you need split settlements, commission deductions or only internal supplier payouts.
5. **International capability:** Verify supported countries, currencies, card networks, settlement timelines and documentation.
6. **Reconciliation:** Make sure payment, refund and settlement reports can map cleanly to booking IDs.
7. **Risk controls:** Evaluate authentication, fraud screening, chargeback handling and the evidence available for disputes.
8. **Settlement terms:** Compare the standard cycle, faster-settlement options, limits and charges.
9. **Integration:** Review APIs, SDKs, plugins, webhooks and compatibility with the booking engine or custom platform. Development teams can explore Cashfree’s APIs and checkout flows through[Dev Studio](https://www.cashfree.com/devstudio) .
10. **Support:** Establish the escalation process for failed high-value bookings, settlement delays and refund issues.

##


Conclusion


A payment gateway for a travel agency should support more than the moment of checkout. Deposits, supplier settlements, cancellations, refunds, international payments, reconciliation and the long gap between booking and travel all affect how the payment system should be designed.


The right choice depends on the agency’s business model, customer mix and supplier relationships. Cashfree Payments brings together Payment Links, Smart Collect, Easy Split, International Payments, Instant Settlements and 180+ payment modes under one platform. Travel businesses should confirm product eligibility, settlement terms and compliance requirements for their specific use case during onboarding.


##


FAQs


#### What is the best payment gateway for a travel agency in India?


The best option is the one that fits the agency’s booking and settlement model. Look for support for deposits, refunds, booking-level reconciliation, relevant payment methods, international collections and split settlements where vendors need to be paid separately. Cashfree Payments provides these capabilities through products including Payment Links, Smart Collect, Easy Split and International Payments.


#### Why can travel businesses be considered high-risk by payment providers?


Travel bookings may be paid for months before fulfilment and can involve high transaction values, cancellations and fraud exposure. These factors create a longer window for disputes and chargebacks. Classification, reserves and pricing ultimately depend on the provider’s underwriting assessment of the individual merchant.


#### How are payments split between suppliers in a package booking?


A split-settlement product can deduct the travel agency’s commission and configure settlements to eligible vendors or partners. With Cashfree Easy Split, businesses can define split rules and access reports for settlements, refunds and adjustments. Vendor onboarding and settlement requirements should be confirmed before integration.


#### Which payment gateway can a travel website use for international bookings?


An Indian travel website should choose a provider with appropriate cross-border authorisation, supported international payment methods and clear settlement documentation. Cashfree’s International Payment Gateway supports eligible international card payments in 140+ currencies and typically settles funds in INR within T+2 business days, subject to merchant approval and applicable terms.


#### How can travel agencies reduce cancellation-related chargebacks?


Publish clear cancellation and refund terms before payment, acknowledge cancellation requests quickly, process eligible refunds promptly and communicate the expected timeline. Keep the booking confirmation, customer consent, refund status and proof of service available in case a dispute is raised.


#### How can a travel website collect a deposit and the remaining balance?


The website can collect the deposit during checkout and later send a separate payment link for the remaining amount. Each payment should carry or map to the same booking reference. Recurring mandates should be used only when the payment arrangement genuinely fits a recurring, customer-authorised collection model.


#### What security standards should a travel payment gateway meet?


Look for PCI DSS compliance, secure card authentication, real-time fraud controls, transaction monitoring and the appropriate regulatory authorisation. The travel business should also secure its own booking system, limit access to payment data and maintain evidence for refund and dispute handling.


#### How do payment gateways integrate with travel booking engines and GDS platforms?


Custom booking engines commonly integrate through payment APIs, SDKs and webhooks. A Global Distribution System or third-party booking platform may require a supported plugin, middleware layer or custom connector. Before selecting a gateway, confirm how payment status, booking confirmation, refunds and settlement references will pass between the systems.
